vibe_typer_batch_3.brief: docs/vibe-typer.kickoff-s4.md, sub-slice B, batch two (the avatars: the user and Sprocket, 128x128, in the chat header beside the names, text as the fallback)

route.via: Comfy Cloud partner_generate (workflow-persist path, Flux2ImageNode), one call per generation. submit_batch was not tried: batch one already established that its medias[] takes a public URL or an uploaded name and not a Comfy output by prompt_id, and every generation here chains from a prompt_id.
route.references: the user's first two takes chained from the accepted bash piece-tile sheet (job 5e350f14-ffef-4e5c-979c-fbd61b05d317), so the portraits sit on the tiles' palette weight and pixel scale, which are in turn the frames' and the logo's. The user's third take chained from its own second take, and Sprocket's first take chained from the accepted user portrait, so the two faces are cousins rather than strangers. Sprocket's second take chained from its own first. The fourth user take chained from the third, on the same change-list shape. The fourth user take chained from the third, on the same change-list shape. The set character started again from the accepted Sprocket portrait, taken for palette weight and pixel scale only because a change list cannot turn one person into another, and its second and third takes chained from the take before.
route.aspect: 1:1 was asked for on every call and the node rendered 1024x768 every time, exactly as 2:1 did in the two batches before this one. It costs nothing here: the cut squares the drawing about its own ink, and every prompt asked for the drawing to sit inside a square area in the middle of the picture for that reason.
route.approved_by: Director: batch two of sub-slice B is the avatars, and the generation count for this batch is open rather than capped, as batch one's was, because the two portraits are the faces of the game and a re-roll that lands is cheaper than a face that does not. Spent six. The user's portrait was re-rolled once more after the Director read it: the tipped plant read as strange rather than chaotic, so the plant went, the desk was cleared to one upright mug and the grin was closed. The open count covered it. The user's portrait was re-rolled twice more after the Director read it. First the tipped plant went, because it read as strange rather than chaotic. Then the character itself was set — the vibe coder is a man with an overgrown beard and a mess of hair — which is a new subject rather than a correction, so it started again from a fresh draw. The open count covered both.
route.spend: 9 generations: seven for the user and two for Sprocket. The user's first character ran 7501 rejected, 7502 rejected, 7503 accepted and then superseded on the Director's read, 7506 accepted and installed and then superseded when the Director set the character; the set character ran 7507 rejected, 7508 rejected, 7509 accepted and installed. Sprocket ran 7504 rejected, 7505 accepted and installed. Two installed, seven not. Nothing else was made in this batch — the milestone cards and the backdrop are later batches on their own approval.

acceptance.cut: a lead-side step, not a generation: apps/cabinets/scripts/cut-avatar.mjs (committed, no dependency). It imports the PNG codec, the ink threshold, the eight per cent margin and squareOf from slice-tiles.mjs rather than copying them, so the two cuts cannot drift apart. It projects the ink onto the two axes, takes the one box the whole drawing sits in, ignores rows and columns with fewer than two lit pixels so a stray speck cannot drag the box out to the whole picture, squares that box about its own center, and area-averages it to 128x128. It leaves the result opaque, because an avatar is drawn on a chat pane painted the same near-black the picture is drawn on. It throws rather than guessing when there is no drawing to find or when the ink fills the frame.
acceptance.readability: looked at both at 128 px and again at 32 px, the size the header shows them at, by area-averaging to 32 and blowing that back up with no smoothing. Both read: the user as a pile of amber hair and beard around a pale face on a navy torso, which at that size is a silhouette and therefore this person rather than a generic one; Sprocket as a dark screen with a face and one amber square under it. The eyes and mouths go soft at 32 on both.

route.via: Comfy Cloud partner_generate (workflow-persist path, Flux2ImageNode), one call per generation. submit_batch was not tried: batch one already established that its medias[] takes a public URL or an uploaded name and not a Comfy output by prompt_id, and every generation here chains from a prompt_id.
route.references: the first six seed-card takes chained from the accepted bash piece-tile sheet (job 5e350f14-ffef-4e5c-979c-fbd61b05d317) or from the take before them, so the cards sit on the tiles' palette weight and pixel scale, which are in turn the frames' and the logo's. The accepted seed card (job 440d18ae, seed 7607) is then the reference for everything after it: the eighth seed take, the series A card, the unicorn card and the deploy ribbon all chain from it, and the unicorn's second take chains from its own first.
route.aspect: the node honors params.width and params.height. This is new, and it corrects what the two batches before this one recorded. Batch one asked for 2:1 and batch two for 1:1 through the tool's top-level aspect_ratio and both were rendered 1024x768, which was written up as 'the node renders 4:3 whatever aspect is asked for'. It does not: params.width and params.height reach Flux2ImageNode and are honored exactly, within 256..2048 on each side in steps of 32. The first six seed takes were generated at the default 1024x768 and fought the crop; the seventh was generated at 1440x480 and did not. The cards are 1440x480 (3:1, an exact 3x downscale to 480x160) and the ribbon is 2048x256 (8:1, an exact 3.2x downscale to 640x80).
route.approved_by: Director: batches three and four of sub-slice B are approved, each with the generation count open as the earlier batches were, because the cards and the ribbon are the moments the game celebrates. Spent thirteen. Eight of those went on the seed card, and seven of the eight were the same fight: a 3:1 banner asked for inside a 4:3 frame either has to be cropped through its own art or has to be drawn small enough to survive the crop, and neither is a thing a change list can fix. The seventh take found the real fix, which was to generate at 3:1, and the three that followed it cost one, two and two.
route.spend: 13 generations that ran, plus one submit that was refused before it ran. The seed card ran 7601 through 7608 (7607 accepted, the other seven rejected); the series A card ran 7609 and was accepted on its first; the unicorn ran 7610 (rejected on contrast) and 7612 (accepted); the ribbon was first submitted at 1280x160, which Flux2ImageNode refused pre-spend because its height minimum is 256, and then ran 7611 (rejected on its ground) and 7613 (accepted) at 2048x256. Seed 7611 therefore appears twice: once on a submit that never reached a GPU and once on the generation that did.

acceptance.glyph_check: ai-eyes image_contains, query "text, letters, numbers or written words", threshold 0.02, on all thirteen generations and on all four installed cuts. The highest score anywhere in the batch is 0.0003, on the installed deploy ribbon, sixty times under the threshold; every other score in the batch is at or below 0.000035. Nothing was over, and nothing needed a re-cut or a re-roll for a glyph. The ribbon's 0.0003 is not a glyph: a long thin band with two parallel lines down it is line-shaped, and line-shaped is part of what that query measures. Looked at at full size there is nothing written on it, which is the whole point of the batch.
acceptance.dimensions: the three cards are exactly 480x160 RGBA and every pixel is alpha 255; the ribbon is exactly 640x80 RGBA with its ground keyed to alpha 0 (23,668 pixels clear, 27,047 solid, 485 on the ramp between). All read off the decoded buffer, not trusted to the encoder.
acceptance.file_size: seed.png 35,005 B, series-a.png 42,832 B, unicorn.png 51,572 B, deployed.png 13,591 B; all four under the 60 KB the brief sets.
acceptance.cut: a lead-side step, not a generation: apps/cabinets/scripts/cut-banner.mjs (committed, no dependency). It imports the PNG codec, the ground, the two key thresholds and the ink box from slice-tiles.mjs and cut-avatar.mjs rather than copying them, so the three cuts in this repo cannot drift apart. Where the drawing sits is a flag rather than an assumption: --frame takes the whole picture, which is what a card and a ribbon generated at their own aspect both are, and without it the ink is hunted for. It fits the named aspect around that box by growing the short side where the picture has room and trimming the long side where it does not, then area-averages down to the named size. All four images here were generated at their own aspect, so all four were cut with --frame and the fit was a no-op to the pixel. The cards are left opaque, because a card is drawn on the page and its own navy IS the card; the ribbon is keyed, because it is drawn over the preview and an opaque ground would punch a band through the device frame and the packed blocks underneath it. It throws rather than guessing when no rectangle at the aspect fits, and when the finished cut carries fewer than four colors.
acceptance.readability: looked at all four at full size and again at the size the field shows them. The cards are shown behind the toast's word at 3:1 and between 28 and 48 px tall, so the badge on the left third is about the size of a chat avatar; all three badges read as what they are at that size, and the right two thirds of every card is empty navy, which is where the word goes. The ribbon is drawn 480 CSS px wide and 60 tall over the preview; its folded ends and its two cream lines survive, and the middle is empty for the word.
acceptance.misses: three, stated rather than rationalized. (1) The amber. The seed card, the unicorn card and the ribbon all came back with an orange where the arcade's warm amber (#e8a04a) was named, and one change list spent on it (7608) went the other way into salmon and was rejected. The orange ships. At the size these are shown it reads as the arcade's amber and it is consistent across all four images, which matters more for a set than the hex does. (2) The cards' navy is not one navy: the three plates measure #17314b, #21384f and #274059 against the #1b2440 named, so the unicorn card's ground is visibly lighter than the seed card's when they are put side by side. They are never shown side by side. (3) The badge interiors differ: the seed card's glow is filled cream behind the plant, while the series A and unicorn badges have a navy middle. The unicorn's navy middle was asked for deliberately, because a cream unicorn on a cream ground disappeared; the seed card's cream middle was not re-rolled to match, and that is a spend decision rather than a design one.

acceptance.tags_family: Calm lo-fi chiptune, instrumental, no vocals, no voice, no singing, no humming, no vocal chops. Mellow and unhurried, a steady relaxed groove with a soft 8-bit drum machine and a gentle bassline. Even dynamics from start to finish: no build, no riser, no drop, no sweep, no ticking, no countdown. Loopable background music for a quiet workspace.
acceptance.no_words: faster-whisper small.en on the rig's GPU over each installed mp3, language en, beam 1, no VAD filter. All seven transcribe to the empty string: nought characters, no word at all. This is the mechanical form of the rule that the field may carry no words a model wrote (G17) — a sung word is a word — and it is why the tags name no vocals, no voice, no singing, no humming and no vocal chops, five ways, rather than once. A real word would have been a miss and a re-roll; none was.
acceptance.duration: every installed bed is exactly 38.000 seconds, 48 kHz, stereo, inside the 36 to 40 the brief sets and matching Ghost's own 36 and 40. The masters were asked for at 52 seconds rather than 38 because ACE-Step writes an intro, a body and a long silent tail: the first job asked for 38 and gave 30.4 seconds of music, which is not a 38 second loop. At 52 the seven bodies run 44.8 to 50.5 seconds and every window fits inside one with room to start a few bars past the opening.
acceptance.loudness: integrated loudness, BS.1770-4, measured in the scratchpad with a K-weighting pair applied in the frequency domain, 400 ms blocks at 75 per cent overlap, absolute gate at -70 LUFS and a relative gate 10 LU under the gated mean. Ghost's menu.mp3 measures -11.59 LUFS on the same code and is the reference the brief names. The seven land between -13.53 and -13.62 LUFS, so the widest distance from Ghost is 2.03 dB and the narrowest 1.94, both inside the 3 dB band. The target was -13.0 and the tanh soft clip that holds the peaks costs about half a decibel of it, which is recorded rather than chased.
acceptance.file_size: 609,024 bytes each, 594.75 KB, under the 700 KB the brief sets and seven of them for 4,263,168 bytes in the package. 128 kbps constant, which is libsndfile's rung below Ghost's own measured ~133 kbps.
acceptance.seam: each installed bed is a bar-aligned window with its last beat folded back over its first at equal power, so the frame after the last frame is the frame that followed it in the master and the loop is continuous in the source. Measured as the one-sample jump from the last frame back to the first against the median jump inside the file: the seven land at 0.22 to 0.66, all under one, where Ghost's menu.mp3 is 30.7 because it hard-loops a file with 4.7 seconds of silence on the end. The head and tail RMS gap is reported per bed and is a weaker reading — csharp's 14.77 dB is two different chords fifty milliseconds either side of a bar line, not a hole. So the shell hard-loops one element per stack, as Ghost does, and the crossfade is spent on stack changes rather than on the loop point.
acceptance.listening: not done and not claimable. Claude cannot hear these; every number above is measured and every judgement of whether a bed is the right music for its stack is the Director's, who hears them from the installed paths.
acceptance.in_the_shell: pnpm build:play puts all seven under site/public/play/vibe/tracks/ at 609,024 bytes each, and pnpm build:launcher puts them in the Vibe package's dist. The pack gate was exercised both ways: with the seven removed from a built dist it halts naming each missing file and exits 1, and with them back it exits 0. The Ghost tarball carries no vibe or keys file at all, read off the file list rather than trusted to the gate.

The chair is in the foreground with its back to the viewer, empty, drawn as one flat dark shape. Beyond it stands a dark desk, and on the desk one computer screen seen from behind and slightly to one side with its light spilling forward: the visible face of the screen is one completely flat plain warm amber (#e8a04a) rectangle with absolutely nothing on it — no picture, no lines, no bars, no icons, no dots and no marks of any kind. Behind the desk is a window looking out on a city at night: a few small square lights scattered across dark towers, and nothing else. One plant in a pot stands beside the desk, and a few plain cables run down from the desk to the floor. The whole room is drawn in deep navy (#1b2440) and near-black (#101018), with slate blue (#6a8aaa) on a few edges; the only warm color anywhere is the amber of the screen and the small amber glow it throws on the desk and on the back of the chair. It is a dark picture on purpose: the middle of the picture, where the screen and the desk are, is the lightest part, and the top edge, the bottom edge, the left edge and the right edge are all deep navy and near-black with nothing bright in them at all. Everything is drawn perfectly flat with hard edges and no shading, seen straight on from behind the chair, with no tilted lines and no dramatic angle. There is no border, no outline, no frame, no box and no panel of any kind around the picture. Hard edges, flat colors, no gradients, no reflections, no noise, no texture, no vignette. No letters, no numbers, no words, no arrows, no symbols, no user interface labels, no text of any kind anywhere in the image.
